authority.document: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1
authority.observation: EED item 3 contains an eight-byte layer-table handle; this text does not explicitly specify byte order.

libreDwgControl.independentTrace: The scratch source object CRC matched, and a separate bit walker located the bytes from the traced type-42 frame.

crossCheck.odaReadOfLibreDwgWholeFile: ODA rejected the scratch file with an AcDbDictionary/AcDbEntity cast error; this does not isolate EED byte-order behavior and is not used as evidence.

conclusions: ODA R13 and R14 producer outputs encode the observed handle big-endian and recover PROBE_LAYER on ODA reopen. Reversing only those eight bytes with a corrected object CRC causes the dictionary layer XDATA to disappear on ODA reopen.
The locally generated LibreDWG control encodes its observed layer handle little-endian; LibreDWG reads the ODA R13 bytes as a different wide integer.
The current libdxfrw reader and DWG encoder use little-endian for this field. A global swap or a 32-bit-size heuristic alone would risk compatibility or misidentify an unresolved wide handle.
limits: These are generated bounded controls, not native AutoCAD witnesses or whole-format support evidence.
The swapped file is a derived negative control, not a producer source.

The evidence does not by itself identify a safe universal rule for conflicting or unresolved references; preserve both physical interpretations and require source/profile and target-identity proof before selection.
